name: Robin Kiln
life: Robin got the sailing place on a very good essay about the sea and had to borrow nearly everything required to reach it. Offering the next pupil a shelf of shoes is a way to improve the award without disparaging the people who made it. People around Maré Coffee know Robin by a small Monday habit. Robin likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: My scholarship covers lessons and nothing you wear to them. I came in borrowed shoes and fell on that step. I want a shelf where the next beginner can borrow a pair that fits.
appearance: Robin is easy to recognize by auburn hair cut square at the nape and a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Usually dressed in a charcoal zip cardigan with one cuff folded back twice, Robin rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
personality: Robin gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Robin privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To stock a shelf of properly fitting loan shoes.
family: Jody Baker is Robin’s first cousin once removed. Robin brings a spare shopping bag. Jody chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Hem by hem*, Jody says, “I thought the small pocket held a ring. It held bus money in case she wanted to leave.”
connections: Ivo Carden (dockside mentor). The student can tell the mechanic what a beginner's foot does on the slippery step.

reactions.situation: A broker offers cash to keep the dock empty
reactions.response: Robin finds out who was promised the empty dock time before discussing a price.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Robin keeps the documents out of view and lets the person claiming it identify it before hearing any details.

reactions.situation: If a colleague lies to save face
reactions.response: Robin offers one private chance to correct it before the next conversation.
